name: NABARD Grade A (Assistant Manager)
conductedBy: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)
tagline: Assistant Manager (RDBS) at NABARD: development banking for agriculture and rural India

overview.about: NABARD recruits Assistant Managers in Grade 'A' for the Rural Development Banking Service (General and specialist disciplines), Legal and Protocol & Security services. The RDBS selection runs through Phase I (objective), Phase II (descriptive + objective) and an interview; Agriculture & Rural Development (ARD) and Economic & Social Issues (ESI) are central.
eligibility: RDBS (General): graduation with 60% (55% for SC/ST/PwBD) or post-graduation with 55% (50% for SC/ST/PwBD), or CA/CS/ICWA, or a full-time MBA/PGDM with 55%; specialist posts need discipline-specific degrees
Age 21–30 years on the date in the notification; relaxation SC/ST 5 yrs, OBC-NCL 3 yrs, PwBD 10–15 yrs
Indian citizen (or other categories as defined)
Check the current advertisement for the exact streams and disciplines on offer

pattern.paper: Phase I — Economic & Social Issues (rural focus)

pattern.note: Merit section; total 200 marks; −0.25 per wrong answer

pattern.paper: Phase II Paper I — General English
Phase II Paper II — ESI & ARD
pattern.note: 50 objective (30 min) + 50 descriptive (90 min) for RDBS General

chapters.title: Pattern & strategy: ARD + ESI decide your rank

cards.title: Qualifying vs merit sections
cards.body: In Phase I, Reasoning, English, Computer, Quant and Decision Making are **qualifying**. **GA (20) + ESI (40) + ARD (40) = 100 marks** decide who goes to Phase II. So ARD and ESI are worth 80% of the merit portion.

cards.title: One preparation for both phases
cards.body: Phase II Paper II tests the **same ESI and ARD** with descriptive answers. Make notes in an answer-ready format (definition, data, issues, way forward) from the start so Phase I and II prep overlap fully.

cards.title: Decision Making
cards.body: 10 marks of situational questions on ethics and organisational judgment. Choose answers that are **lawful, fair, consultative and farmer-centric**, avoiding both inaction and rule-breaking.

cards.title: Data sources
cards.body: Use the Economic Survey (agriculture and social chapters), Union Budget, NABARD's annual report, PIB releases on the Ministries of Agriculture and Rural Development, and the latest Agriculture Census data.

cards.q: In NABARD Grade A Phase I, which sections form the merit portion?
cards.explain: GA + ESI + ARD (100 marks) decide shortlisting; the rest are qualifying.

cards.q: How many marks does the NABARD Grade A interview carry?
cards.explain: The interview carries 50 marks; it is added to Phase II for final merit.

cards.title: Land holding classes
points: Marginal + small holdings: over 85% of all holdings

cards.title: Crops & seasons
points: Kharif (monsoon): rice, maize, cotton, soybean, groundnut
India: world's largest producer of milk and pulses

cards.title: Rural development schemes
cards.body: **MGNREGA** (Act 2005): up to **100 days** of guaranteed wage work per rural household a year. **DAY-NRLM** (2011): livelihoods through **self-help groups**. **PMAY-G**: rural housing. **PMKSY** (2015): 'Har Khet Ko Pani', 'More crop per drop'.

cards.title: Agricultural credit
cards.body: **KCC** for short-term crop loans; interest subvention gives eligible farmers loans at 7% (effective 4% with prompt repayment). **NABARD** refinances banks, manages the **RIDF** (since 1995-96) and promotes SHG–bank linkage (since 1992).

cards.title: Allied sectors
cards.body: Animal husbandry, dairy, fisheries and poultry now contribute a large and growing share of agricultural GVA. Know **Operation Flood** (1970, NDDB), the **Blue Revolution**, and schemes like **PM Matsya Sampada Yojana** (fisheries) and the **Rashtriya Gokul Mission** (indigenous cattle).

cards.q: A farmer owning 1.5 hectares is classified as:
MGNREGA guarantees up to how many days of wage employment per rural household per year?
cards.explain: The Act guarantees up to 100 days of wage employment per household per financial year.

cards.q: The SHG–Bank Linkage Programme was launched by NABARD in:
cards.explain: NABARD started the SHG–Bank Linkage pilot in 1992.

chapters.title: ESI (rural focus) & NABARD as an institution

cards.title: NABARD in brief
cards.body: Established **12 July 1982** under the NABARD Act, 1981, on the recommendation of the **CRAFICARD (B. Sivaraman) committee**. Wholly owned by the **Government of India**. Roles: refinance, development (watershed, tribal development, FPOs), and **supervision** of RRBs and cooperative banks.

cards.title: Poverty & inequality
cards.body: Earlier poverty lines: **Tendulkar** (2009) and **Rangarajan** (2014) committees. NITI Aayog's **Multidimensional Poverty Index** uses health, education and living standards (12 indicators in India's version). Inequality is measured with the **Gini coefficient**.

cards.title: Demography & social issues
cards.body: **Demographic dividend**: growth potential when the working-age share is high. Key ESI themes: rural–urban migration, women's labour-force participation, social security for informal workers, nutrition, and education quality.

cards.title: Writing ESI answers
cards.body: Open with a definition and one data point, then cover causes/issues, government measures (named schemes), and a way forward with 3–4 points. Keep each descriptive answer tied to rural India, since that is NABARD's mandate.

cards.q: NABARD was set up on the recommendation of:
cards.explain: The CRAFICARD committee, chaired by B. Sivaraman, recommended NABARD.

cards.q: Which institution supervises RRBs and cooperative banks on behalf of RBI?
cards.explain: NABARD carries out supervision of RRBs and state/district cooperative banks.
